newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The new minority bloc in the Senate elected former Senate president Neptali Gonzales as the new Senate minority leader and pledged to oppose any moves to amend the Constitution to lift the term limits of government officials (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Senators who staged a coup at the Senate last month plan to oust House Speaker Jose de Venecia and replace him with Rep Raul Daza of Samar (MALAYA)
- Investments registered with the Board of Investments dropped by 60 percent to 90.93 billion pesos in the first eight months this year from the year-ago 225.658 billion pesos (BULLETIN)

- U.S.-based investment firm Goldman Sachs said it expected the Philippine peso to weaken to 26.40 to the U.S. dollar by the end of this year, and further to a 27.30-peso in the next 12 months. The peso ended at 26.28 on Friday. (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- The Philippines was held up as one of the few if not the only Asian country to buck a regional economic slowdown and was rated by the Political and Economic Risk Consultancy to be the possible "flavor of the year" for investors (INQUIRER)
- The Bases Conversion Development Authority and the Fil-Estate Management/Penta Capital consortium have tentatively set the signing of the Club John Hay lease agreement on Oct 19 (INQUIRER)
- The Senate coup is another unnecessary change that will distract trade and investment, aside from further delaying the approval of important economic bills, businessmen said. (BUSINESSWORLD).
